proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide that is widely used as a LiCoO2 cathode coating. It is reasonably stable against high-voltage oxide cathodes at 4.0 V and has modest chemical compatibility with sulfide electrolytes, so it is a strong baseline for the interface criteria.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich halide with high oxidative stability, so it should resist decomposition against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. Its fluoride anion is not expected to be reduced or to exchange chemically with the PS4 and Cl framework of Li6PS5Cl, which suggests a lower sulfide contact penalty than the Li3PO4 baseline, whose P2O5/SO2 products dominated the penalty. It also moves to the halide family, which is a different chemistry from the phosphate baseline.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom (bin 16, not acceptable) from a reaction with Li6PS5Cl that released P2O5, SCl4 and SO2, so a coating chemically different from the phosphate is needed.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich orthoborate with strong B-O bonding. Its oxidative stability should resist LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and its Li-rich, low-Lewis-acidity framework may avoid the P2O5/SO2/SCl-type sulfur products that drove the penalties of Li3PO4 and LiF. It also belongs to the borate family, which has not been tested yet.
